 This Crl.P, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The Court
Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioner-accused No.1 is before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.
151/2022 of Byndoor Police Station, pending on the file of the learned Principal Civil Judge and JMFC Kundapura (Itinerary) Byndoor Udupi District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 465, 468, 471, 420 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant - B Rama Kharvi.
2. Heard Sri. Jayantha Poojary, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Rahul Rai K, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"
NC: 2024:KHC:20921

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioner being accused No.1 is before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail on the apprehension of being arrested.

The complainant being the Director of the Co- operative Society lodged the first information against accused Nos.1 to 4 alleging that accused Nos. 1 to 3 have formed a trust and started lending money to self help groups on the interest at the rate of 14% per annum.
But they were availing loan from the Nationalized Bank at 10% by suppressing the said fact and retaining the passbooks and the cheque books provided by the Bank.
They used fake seals, created fake beneficiaries and thereby misappropriated huge amount.
It is also said that the accused had kept the borrowers in dark about all these facts.
The allegations made against the petitioner and other accused are serious in nature and they are required for interrogation.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
